text:
Pavel Buchnevich's ice time is slipping in St. Louis. Over his last ten games he has averaged about a minute less than before, and the production has followed: 3 points in that stretch, 9 in 21 games overall, below his scoring rate from last season.

The case for patience is in the process. The Blues control play with him on, 54.2% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances), 4.4 points better than without him, and the luck around him is neutral: his team has scored almost exactly what its chances deserved with him on. His own shooting, 11.1%, sits at the very bottom of our range for him, so a few more of his looks going in would not be a surprise.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, which is the other side of the argument. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him a signature worth watching: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. Our range for his season is 33 to 51 points; what we'd watch is whether the minutes come back.
